blocks.content: Course: React Hooks: Level Up Your First Web App
Here's what changed from the previous lesson:

items: App now has a refreshKey state (starts at 0). It lives in the useEffect() dependency array, replacing [].
A Refresh button in the entry list header calls setRefreshKey() on click. React detects the change and re-runs the effect.

The error display changed from a single

to an error-banner div with two child paragraphs.
Header and EntryCard are unchanged from the previous lesson.

blocks.content: The Refresh button works because refreshKey is in the dependency array.
But what happens when a value the effect uses is not in the list?
That's the most common mistake when working with useEffect(), and I have a story from my early days that shows just how subtle it can get.
Use this space for your doubts about this lesson. Ask us anything that's confusing and our experts will provide explanations to help you understand.
